You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Final answer format. First list the passages you rely on, copied VERBATIM from the files (no
  paraphrase, no ellipsis inside the quotation marks), then write the answer using only them:
  <evidence>
  [E1] "exact text" (file)
  [E2] "exact text" (file)
  </evidence>
  <answer>
  Your answer to the user. End every factual sentence with the evidence it rests on, e.g. [E1] or
  [E1, E2]. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no marker.
  </answer>
- The user sees only the <answer> part, so it must be complete and readable on its own.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

Briefly identify and explain the parts of section 2015 related to water.


In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

50	DWSRF program through annual appropriations.
    51	From FY1997 through FY2018, Congress appropriated over $23.33 billion for the DWSRF
    52	program. The appropriation for DWSRF program generally ranged between $820.0 million in
    53	FY2000 and $1.39 billion in FY2010.26
    54	DWSRF Program Revisions (AWIA Sections 2002, 2015, and 2022)
    55	AWIA makes the most substantial revisions to the DWSRF provisions of SDWA since the
    56	program was authorized in 1996. These revisions expand the eligible uses of DWSRF financial
    57	assistance, provide states with additional flexibility to administer the DWSRF program, and
    58	include provisions intended to make DWSRF assistance more accessible to public water
    59	systems.
    60	27
    61	AWIA Section 2015(a) amends SDWA to expressly state that DWSRF funds can be used for
    62	projects to replace or rehabilitate aging treatment, storage, or distribution systems.28 Under EPA
    63	guidance, these replacement and rehabilitation projects have been eligible for financial assistance
    64	from the DWSRF if needed to protect public health. According to EPA’s needs survey, this
    65	category of projects accounts for 66.1% of the estimated drinking water infrastructure need.29
    66	Prior to AWIA, these activities were not previously explicitly identified in statute.30
    67	Section 2015 also revises existing DWSRF provisions that address financial assistance for
    68	disadvantaged communities. These amendments increase the portion of a state’s capitalization
    69	grant that states may dedicate to additional subsidization and extend the amortization period for
    70	loans made to disadvantaged communities. Before AWIA, states could use 30% of their annual
    71	capitalization grants to subsidize loans for disadvantaged communities.31 Section 2015(c) of
    72	AWIA increases that proportion to 35% while conditionally requiring states to use at least 6% of
    73	their capitalization grant for these subsidies.32 The section also amends the SDWA DWSRF
    74	provisions to extend the amortization period for loans made to disadvantaged communities from
    75	30 to 40 years.
    76	Section 2015(d) of AWIA also extends the repayment and amortization period for all projects
    77	financed by the DWSRF. Previously, SDWA required DWSRF financing recipients to pay the
    78	initial principal and interest payments within one year of project completion. This amendment
    79	extends the date of that initial payment to 18 months after project completion. This section also
    80	authorizes the extension of the amortization period for projects that receive DWSRF assistance
    81	from 20 to 30 years.
    82	Section 2015(e) requires EPA to evaluate and include the cost to replace lead service lines in the
    83	drinking water infrastructure needs survey, which EPA completes every four years.33 EPA uses the
    84	needs survey to allot the DWSRF appropriation among the states.
    85	34 In conducting the needs
    86	survey, EPA has not previously requested that public water systems report the cost to replace
    87	these lines.35 AWIA specifies that the cost to replace lead lines must be included in the needs
    88	survey (to the extent practicable), which may potentially affect some states’ allotments of
    89	DWSRF capitalization grants.
    90	Section 2015(g) of AWIA requires EPA to gather specified information on DWSRF
    91	administration from state drinking water administrators and report to Congress on best practices
    92	for implementing the DWSRF to facilitate the application process and to improve DWSRF
    93	financial management and sustainability.
    94	Source Water Assessment and Protection
    95	In 1996, Congress added source water assessment provisions to SDWA to encourage protection of
    96	drinking water sources.
    97	36 Section 1453 required states to develop source water assessment
    98	programs that delineate areas from which public water systems receive water and identify the
    99	origins of regulated contaminants to determine threats to water systems. States were authorized to
   100	fund these activities from 10% of their DWSRF capitalization grant for FY1996 and FY1997.37
   101	Section 2015(f) of AWIA removes this fiscal year limitation and accordingly authorizes states to
   102	use a portion of their capitalization grant to fund these source water assessments or update an
   103	existing source water assessment.38
   104	The 1996 SDWA amendments required states to conduct source water assessments as a condition
   105	of adopting modified monitoring requirements.
   106	39 However, the 1996 amendments did not
   107	authorize states to fund implementation of source water protection plans from their DWSRF
   108	capitalization grants. AWIA Section 2002 authorizes states to fund implementation of surface
   109	drinking water sources protection efforts and activities from the 10% set-aside of a state’s annual
   110	DWSRF capitalization grant.

According to EPA’s needs survey, this category of projects accounts for 66.1% of the estimated drinking water infrastructure need.29 Prior to AWIA, these activities were not previously explicitly identified in statute.30" (doc.txt)
[E2] "Section 2015 also revises existing DWSRF provisions that address financial assistance for disadvantaged communities. (doc.txt)
[E3] "Section 2015(d) of AWIA also extends the repayment and amortization period for all projects financed by the DWSRF. Previously, SDWA required DWSRF financing recipients to pay the initial principal and interest payments within one year of project completion. This amendment extends the date of that initial payment to 18 months after project completion. This section also authorizes the extension of the amortization period for projects that receive DWSRF assistance from 20 to 30 years." (doc.txt)
[E4] "Section 2015(e) requires EPA to evaluate and include the cost to replace lead service lines in the drinking water infrastructure needs survey, which EPA completes every four years.33 EPA uses the needs survey to allot the DWSRF appropriation among the states." (doc.txt)
[E5] "Section 2015(g) of AWIA requires EPA to gather specified information on DWSRF administration from state drinking water administrators and report to Congress on best practices for implementing the DWSRF to facilitate the application process and to improve DWSRF financial management and sustainability." (doc.txt)
[E6] "Section 2015(f) of AWIA removes this fiscal year limitation and accordingly authorizes states to use a portion of their capitalization grant to fund these source water assessments or update an existing source water assessment.38" (doc.txt)
</evidence>

<answer>
Section 2015 of AWIA (as described in doc.txt) makes revisions to the DWSRF (Drinking Water State Revolving Fund) provisions of SDWA, and every part of it concerns drinking water:

- **Section 2015(a)**: Amends SDWA to expressly state that DWSRF funds can be used for projects to replace or rehabilitate aging treatment, storage, or distribution systems; these projects had been eligible under EPA guidance if needed to protect public health, and this category accounts for 66.1% of the estimated drinking water infrastructure need [E1].
- **Section 2015(c)**: Revises DWSRF provisions for financial assistance to disadvantaged communities, increasing the portion of a state's capitalization grant usable for loan subsidization from 30% to 35% (with a conditional requirement to use at least 6% for these subsidies) and extending the loan amortization period from 30 to 40 years [E2].
- **Section 2015(d)**: Extends the repayment and amortization period for all DWSRF-financed projects, moving the initial principal and interest payment from one year to 18 months after project completion and authorizing extension of the amortization period from 20 to 30 years [E3].
- **Section 2015(e)**: Requires EPA to evaluate and include the cost to replace lead service lines in the drinking water infrastructure needs survey, which EPA uses to allot the DWSRF appropriation among states [E4].
- **Section 2015(f)**: Removes a fiscal year limitation, authorizing states to use a portion of their capitalization grant to fund source water assessments or update an existing one [E6].
- **Section 2015(g)**: Requires EPA to gather specified information on DWSRF administration from state drinking water administrators and report to Congress on best practices for implementing the DWSRF to facilitate the application process and improve DWSRF financial management and sustainability [E5].
</answer>
